title: Interest Rate Quest

walkthroughs.body_html: Simple interest = Principal × Rate × Time. Save £2,000 at 5% for 3 years: 2000 × 0.05 × 3 = £300 interest. Final balance £2,300. Easy for short-term savings.

Compound adds each year's interest to the principal. £1,000 at 10% for 3 years: Year 1 → £1,100. Year 2 → £1,210. Year 3 → £1,331. Compare with simple: £1,300. Compound earned £31 extra. Over decades the gap balloons.
Bank Rate jumps 0.5%. A £200,000 mortgage costs roughly £1,000 more per year (£200,000 × 0.005). Households cut other spending — AD falls. Savers gain. Trade-off: slower growth, but lower inflation.
